# 2025 Tour Championship
## Background and Context
The 2025 Tour Championship was the final event of the PGA Tour’s 2025 FedEx Cup Playoffs and marked the conclusion of the 2024–25 PGA Tour season. It followed two playoff tournaments—the FedEx St. Jude Championship and the BMW Championship—as part of the three-event postseason series leading to the FedEx Cup. Players accumulated points throughout the season to qualify for the playoffs, with the top 70 advancing to the first event, 50 moving on to the second, and the remaining top 30 in the FedEx Cup standings qualifying for the Tour Championship. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler entered the playoffs as the FedEx Cup points leader and was the top seed at East Lake, followed by Rory McIlroy, J.J. Spaun, Justin Rose, and Tommy Fleetwood as the top five in points.
The playoff race leading into the Tour Championship featured dramatic moments. Justin Rose won the FedEx St. Jude Championship in a playoff, vaulting from 25th to 4th in the standings. In the second leg, Scottie Scheffler captured the BMW Championship at Caves Valley, solidifying his No. 1 position heading to East Lake. These victories set the stage for a tightly packed field of 30 elite players competing for the FedEx Cup title. Six former FedEx Cup champions were among the qualifiers, including defending cup holder Scheffler, Viktor Hovland, McIlroy, Patrick Cantlay, Rose, and Justin Thomas. Notably, Fleetwood came in as one of only two players in the field without a PGA Tour win to date (alongside rookie Jacob Bridgeman), a fact that foreshadowed the historic breakthrough to come.
## Location and Course Details
The tournament was played at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, Georgia, the long-standing host venue of the Tour Championship. East Lake is a historic course (the home club of legendary golfer Bobby Jones) and has hosted the Tour Championship continuously since 2004 (and also in 1998, 2000, 2002). The course is a par 70, measuring 7,440 yards for the tournament setup. It is a classical parkland-style layout originally designed by Tom Bendelow and later reworked by Donald Ross, with a significant renovation completed prior to the 2024 event by architect Andrew Green. The 2023 renovation included reshaped bunkers, some tree removal, and the conversion of all greens to Bermuda grass, making many greens larger and more undulating. Notably, the club had briefly played as par 71 in 2024 but returned to a par-70 configuration for 2025, featuring just two par-five holes. East Lake’s turf is known for its Zoysia grass fairways and thick Bermudagrass rough, placing a premium on accuracy off the tee. The course’s record score is 257 (23-under-par) set by Tiger Woods in 2007, with the single-round record of 60 held by Zach Johnson.
## Format and Field Qualification
Starting in 2025, the Tour Championship format underwent a significant change. The PGA Tour eliminated the staggered “starting strokes” system that had been used from 2019 through 2024 to give the FedEx Cup points leader a head-start in scoring. Instead, all 30 players began the tournament at even par, and the Tour Championship was played as a standard 72-hole stroke-play event. Whoever had the lowest 72-hole score would be crowned the tournament winner and FedEx Cup champion, making for a more straightforward and engaging competition. There was no cut, as is customary in this small-field event.
The field comprised the top 30 players in the FedEx Cup standings after the BMW Championship. Thanks to their season-long performance, each of these players earned a two-year PGA Tour exemption (through 2026) for reaching the Tour Championship, if not already exempt. The elite field included many of the season’s top performers and multiple major champions. Six players in the field were past FedEx Cup champions, underlining the strength of competition. At the same time, several players qualified without winning any PGA Tour event that season, relying on consistent high finishes. In fact, Tommy Fleetwood entered East Lake at 5th in points despite not having won on Tour in 2025. With the reset to even par for all, every qualifier had a mathematical chance to win the FedEx Cup over four rounds, adding intrigue for lower-ranked players. Scottie Scheffler, as the No. 1 seed and reigning FedEx Cup champion, was aiming to become the first ever to win back-to-back FedEx Cups, while veterans like McIlroy (a three-time FedEx Cup winner) and younger contenders like Ludvig Åberg and Akshay Bhatia looked to challenge for the title. The new format promised a “level playing field,” echoing PGA Tour Commissioner Jay Monahan’s goal of a more fan-friendly and climactic finish to the season.
## Tournament Summary
### Round 1 (Thursday, August 21)
Russell Henley blazed out to the first-round lead with a bogey-free 9-under-par 61, an opening salvo that put him two strokes ahead of the field. Henley, a Georgia native playing in front of home-state fans, tallied seven birdies and an eagle on East Lake’s receptive greens. His 61 was one shot shy of the course record and was the lowest round of the tournament. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler started strong with a 63 (−7) despite a late scare from a wayward drive on 16, ending the day alone in second place. Five players were tied at 6-under 64, three shots off the lead, in a logjam for third. This group at 64 included Tommy Fleetwood, Patrick Cantlay, Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, and Scotland’s Robert MacIntyre, all of whom capitalized on soft conditions and a “lift, clean and place” setup to go low. Reigning FedEx Cup champ Rory McIlroy opened with a 66 (−4) and was part of a tie for 8th, while several other contenders lurked just a few strokes back. In total, 21 of the 30 players broke par in the opening round as East Lake yielded unusually low scoring for a Tour Championship start.
### Round 2 (Friday, August 22)
Tommy Fleetwood surged into a share of the 36-hole lead, continuing his quest for an elusive first PGA Tour win. Fleetwood followed his first-round 64 with a 7-under 63 in the second round, highlighted by six birdies on the back nine, to reach 13-under-par overall. He was joined at the top by overnight leader Russell Henley, who posted a solid 4-under 66 to also sit at 13-under through two rounds. The co-leaders enjoyed a two-shot cushion heading into the weekend. The low round of Friday came from Cameron Young, who vaulted himself into contention with a blistering 62 (−8). Young’s round featured nine birdies, including a run of five birdies in six holes on the back nine, moving him to 11-under and alone in third place after 36 holes. Close behind, Patrick Cantlay and Robert MacIntyre were tied for fourth at 10-under following matching rounds of 64, keeping within striking distance of the lead. In contrast, Scottie Scheffler lost a bit of ground on day two; after a 69, he stood at 8-under (five shots back) at the tournament’s midway point. A large pack of players remained in the mix, with a dozen competitors clustered between 7-under and 10-under, including major winners like Shane Lowry (who shot 63 Friday to reach −7) and Rory McIlroy (−7). With soft conditions persisting but pin positions growing tougher, the stage was set for a tightly contested weekend battle for the FedEx Cup.
### Round 3 (Saturday, August 23)
Moving day saw the tournament tighten up as conditions toughened under cloudy, drizzly skies. Patrick Cantlay shot a superb 6-under 64 in the third round to leap into a tie for the lead by day’s end. Cantlay, a former FedEx Cup champion, carded seven birdies on Saturday to erase a three-shot deficit. He joined 36-hole leader Tommy Fleetwood at 16-under-par (194) total, as Fleetwood grinded out a 67 despite some mid-round adversity. Fleetwood stumbled with a bogey at the long par-3 9th and a double bogey at the par-3 15th (after finding the water), but he rebounded with clutch play down the stretch to stay in front. The co-leaders, at 16-under, were two shots clear of Russell Henley, who slipped to third at 14-under after an even-par 70 in Round 3. Making the biggest move on Saturday was Keegan Bradley, who fired the day’s low score, a 7-under 63, to jump into fourth place at 13-under. Bradley began the round three back and briefly surged up the leaderboard, though he remained three strokes off the lead entering Sunday. Scheffler had an up-and-down round (1-under 69) marked by early bogeys, ending the day in fifth at 12-under and still within four of the top. In all, 14 players were within eight shots of the lead heading into the final round, but scoring was notably tougher in Round 3 (the field averaged 69.6 strokes, compared to the mid-67 averages of the first two days) as tournament officials tucked pins and the rain-softened course played longer. With Fleetwood and Cantlay both seeking to end victory droughts, and Henley and others in striking range, the FedEx Cup and $10 million prize were still very much up for grabs.
### Round 4 (Sunday, August 24)
The final round delivered high drama before Tommy Fleetwood ultimately clinched a long-awaited victory. Starting Sunday tied for the lead, Fleetwood and Cantlay dueled through the front nine with neither pulling away. Fleetwood stumbled with a bogey at the 10th hole, which cut his lead to a single stroke over a charging Cantlay. However, the Englishman responded emphatically with back-to-back birdies on the 12th and 13th holes, regaining a comfortable cushion. As the pressure mounted on the closing holes at East Lake, Cantlay could not keep pace. The 2021 FedEx Cup champion bogeyed the par-4 16th, a misstep that effectively ended his comeback bid as Fleetwood maintained a multi-shot margin. Tommy Fleetwood capped off the week with a steady even-par 70 (2-under 68 when adjusted for par), posting a winning total of 18-under-par 262. He finished three strokes ahead of runners-up Russell Henley and Patrick Cantlay, who each concluded at 15-under 265. The victory marked Fleetwood’s first career PGA Tour title and made him the FedEx Cup champion for 2025. It was a breakthrough moment for the 34-year-old, coming in his 164th PGA Tour start after numerous close calls. Fleetwood became the first player since Chad Campbell in 2003 to have his maiden PGA Tour win occur at the Tour Championship.
Behind the winner, the battle for high finishes provided plenty of excitement. Corey Conners carded a blistering 8-under 62 on Sunday – the low round of the final day – vaulting the Canadian into a tie for fourth place at 14-under. Conners’ bogey-free 62 matched Henley’s opening 61 as the best rounds of the week in relation to par. Joining Conners in T-4 were Scottie Scheffler and Cameron Young, also at 14-under 266. Scheffler’s hopes of a repeat FedEx Cup title were effectively dashed after an out-of-bounds tee shot on the first hole led to an early bogey on Sunday, and a double bogey at the 15th removed any outside chance. He closed with 68 to extend his streak of top-10 finishes to 14 consecutive events, but it was only enough for a tie for fourth. Cameron Young bounced back from a shaky third round to shoot 4-under 66 in the finale, also finishing three shots shy of the podium. Rounding out the top ten, players such as Keegan Bradley, Justin Rose, Robert MacIntyre, and Shane Lowry were further down the leaderboard, with Bradley fading to a tie for seventh at 12-under after an even-par final round. In total, 27 of the 30 competitors ended the tournament under par, reflecting both the scorable early conditions and the caliber of the field. When the last putt dropped, it was Tommy Fleetwood hoisting the FedEx Cup trophy, completing a storybook week by shedding the label of “best player without a PGA Tour win” and etching his name in season-ending glory.
## Final Leaderboard and Statistics
Top five finishers: (72-hole aggregate score and relation to par)
1. Tommy Fleetwood – 262 (−18)
T2. Russell Henley – 265 (−15)
T2. Patrick Cantlay – 265 (−15)
T4. Scottie Scheffler – 266 (−14)
T4. Corey Conners – 266 (−14)
T4. Cameron Young – 266 (−14)
Fleetwood’s winning score of 18-under tied the second-lowest in Tour Championship history (though well shy of the record −23) and made him the FedEx Cup Champion for 2025. The lowest round of the tournament was Henley’s opening 61 (−9) on Thursday, which was one stroke off the East Lake course record. Two other rounds of 62 were recorded during the week (Young in round 2 and Conners in round 4). Henley’s 54-hole total of 193 (−17) set a new personal best, though he could not hang on in the final round. The tough 235-yard 15th hole (par 3) played a pivotal role, yielding several double bogeys (including to Fleetwood and Bradley on Saturday) and playing as one of the hardest holes of the week. There were no holes-in-one during the event, but Scottie Scheffler did extend an impressive streak with his T-4 finish: it was his 14th straight top-10, tying a PGA Tour record that had stood since 1977. By winning, Fleetwood earned a five-year PGA Tour exemption (through 2030) and moved to a career-high year-end ranking. He also became the first Englishman to win the FedEx Cup, joining Justin Rose (2018) as the only Europeans to have done so.
## Prize Purse and Points Distribution
The 2025 Tour Championship featured a prize fund of $40 million, reflecting a revamped payout structure tied to the format change. The winner’s share for the FedEx Cup champion was $10 million – a hefty sum, though notably a reduction from the $18–$25 million top prizes of recent years under the old system. Fleetwood collected the entire $10 million bonus with his victory, more than doubling his season’s PGA Tour earnings. Runner-up finishers Henley and Cantlay still earned multi-million dollar bonuses (roughly $6 million and $5 million respectively, based on the FedExCup payout structure), with every player in the Tour Championship field guaranteed at least a six-figure bonus payout. The total FedExCup bonus pool remained $100 million for 2025, but a larger portion of it was allocated to players outside the top 30 compared to prior years, as the Tour Championship itself was treated as a standard event purse. In a significant change, the $40 million Tour Championship purse was counted as official money on the PGA Tour for the first time since 2018. This meant that Fleetwood’s $10 million prize is reflected in official earnings and the all-time money list, whereas under the previous format FedEx Cup bonuses were separate from official money.
No additional FedEx Cup points were awarded during the Tour Championship, since it was the final event determining the season champion. The FedEx Cup standings for 2025 were finalized based on the finishing order at East Lake (with Fleetwood finishing 1st in points). By making the Tour Championship field, all 30 players earned exemptions into the 2026 Masters Tournament and U.S. Open, among other perks, and those who had not already won on tour secured two-year PGA Tour status by virtue of reaching East Lake. The postseason format, with no strokes-based head start, ensured that the $10 million FedEx Cup prize was truly up for grabs at the Tour Championship, rewarding the player who performed best over those four days. The Tour has indicated that this balanced bonus distribution and “winner-take-all” finale will continue to evolve in future seasons to further reward season-long excellence while preserving the drama of the final tournament.
## Broadcast and Media Coverage
The Tour Championship received extensive media coverage and was broadcast to a global audience. In the United States, television coverage was shared by Golf Channel and NBC Sports. Golf Channel provided live coverage of the first two rounds and early coverage on the weekend, while NBC carried the high-profile afternoon broadcasts on Saturday and Sunday, including the decisive back-nine action in the final round. For example, NBC’s Sunday coverage aired from 1:30 p.m. to 6 p.m. ET, following Golf Channel’s lead-in telecast. Viewers in the U.S. could also stream the tournament online. PGA Tour Live on ESPN+ offered featured group coverage and bonus feeds throughout all four days, and NBC’s Peacock service simulcast the NBC broadcast window on the weekend.
In the United Kingdom, Sky Sports Golf held the broadcast rights for the FedEx Cup finale. Sky Sports provided live coverage each day of the tournament in prime time (UK time), given the five-hour time difference with Atlanta. For instance, the first groups on Thursday teed off at 4:26 p.m. BST, with Sky’s live coverage beginning at 6 p.m. BST to capture the late afternoon and evening play in the UK. Internationally, the Tour Championship was covered by the PGA Tour’s world feed partners, ensuring fans in all major golf markets could follow the action. Major golf media outlets like ESPN, CBS Sports, and Golf Channel provided on-site reporting and analysis throughout the week. The compelling storyline of Fleetwood’s quest for his first win garnered significant attention in sports media; even prominent athletes such as LeBron James and Tiger Woods took to social media to congratulate Fleetwood on his breakthrough FedEx Cup victory. With strong viewership and engagement, the 2025 Tour Championship’s broadcast underscored the event’s status as one of the most significant and anticipated tournaments of the year, bringing the PGA Tour season to an exciting close.

In the United Kingdom, Sky Sports Golf held the broadcast rights for the FedEx Cup finale.
Sky Sports provided live coverage each day of the tournament in prime time (UK time), given the five-hour time difference with Atlanta.
For instance, the first groups on Thursday teed off at 4:26 p.m. BST, with Sky’s live coverage beginning at 6 p.m. BST to capture the late afternoon and evening play in the UK.
Internationally, the Tour Championship was covered by the PGA Tour’s world feed partners, ensuring fans in all major golf markets could follow the action.
Major golf media outlets like ESPN, CBS Sports, and Golf Channel provided on-site reporting and analysis throughout the week.

The compelling storyline of Fleetwood’s quest for his first win garnered significant attention in sports media; even prominent athletes such as LeBron James and Tiger Woods took to social media to congratulate Fleetwood on his breakthrough FedEx Cup victory.

With strong viewership and engagement, the 2025 Tour Championship’s broadcast underscored the event’s status as one of the most significant and anticipated tournaments of the year, bringing the PGA Tour season to an exciting close.

![Image 2: A Tour Championship flag is pictured on green at East Lake.](https://golf.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/tour-championship-flag-watch.jpg)

The FedEx Cup title will be decided at the 2025 Tour Championship.

Getty Images

The 2025 Tour Championship, the finale of the [FedEx Cup Playoffs](https://golf.com/news/2025-fedex-cup-explainer-schedule-format/), kicks off this week at [East Lake](https://coursefinder.golf.com/course-profile/2157-East-Lake-Golf-Club/#lat=33.7434825,long=-84.3027121,4.00z) in Atlanta. Here’s everything you need to know to watch the tournament, including a full Tour Championship TV schedule, streaming info and complete tee times for the first and second rounds once they are released.

### How to watch Tour Championship

After a long season that began all the way back in January, we’ve reached the final PGA Tour tournament of the year (at least until the FedEx Cup Fall Series). That also means it’s the last time we’ll see all the best Tour pros tee it up in the same event until the 2025 Ryder Cup in late September.

None of those pros are better than [Scottie Scheffler](https://golf.com/news/was-scottie-scheffler-punished-rules/). The World No. 1 missed the start of the season due to a freak injury, but once he returned, he quickly took hold and started to dominate.

Scheffler has won five times heading into the Tour Championship, including [last week’s BMW Championship](https://golf.com/news/scottie-schefflers-soul-stealing-chip-in-was-different-in-all-the-right-ways/). He’s already raked in two major titles and many millions in FedEx Cup bonus money in 2025. This week, he’ll fight for the winner’s share of the [$40 million Tour Championship purse](https://golf.com/news/fedex-cup-payout-changes-100-million/), hoping to add $10 million more to his coffers.

Scottie Scheffler’s unbelievable chip-in leads Shots of the Week
----------------------------------------------------------------

Check out the best shots of the week from the 2025 BMW Championship, including Akshay Bhatia’s incredible hole-in-one and Scottie Scheffler’s chip-in birdie on the 71st hole.

But Scheffler’s success so far will have no impact in the outcome this week. Unlike at last year’s Tour Championship when Scheffler started at 10 under, players will not receive starting strokes based on FedEx Cup position at East Lake this year.

Instead, Scheffler will start at even par just like the rest of the 30-player field, and it will be a four-round free-for-all for the FedEx Cup title.

That means anyone in the field — including [Rory McIlroy](https://golf.com/news/rory-mcilroy-fedex-cup-playoffs-rule/), [Justin Thomas](https://golf.com/news/justin-thomas-explains-scottie-scheffler-dominance/), [Tommy Fleetwood](https://golf.com/news/tommy-fleetwood-latest-heartbreak-interview/), [Justin Rose](https://golf.com/news/justin-rose-fedex-st-jude-championship-witb/) and even [Akshay Bhatia in 30th place](https://www.pgatour.com/fedexcup) — could steal the Cup from Scheffler’s grasp with one great week. If Scheffler can triumph for the sixth time this season, he’ll win his second consecutive FedEx Cup title.

NBC and Golf Channel will provide TV coverage of the 2025 Tour Championship, while [PGA Tour Live on ESPN+](https://go.web.plus.espn.com/c/3208296/931309/9070) will carry the primary streaming coverage online. [Peacock](https://fave.co/45l5EmB) will carry additional streaming coverage, including simulcasts of NBC’s TV broadcasts on the weekend.

You can find complete information about streaming or watching the tournament on TV below.

### Tournament basics

**What:** 2025 Tour Championship  
**Where:** East Lake Golf Club, Atlanta, Ga.  
**When:** Thursday-Sunday, Aug. 21-24  
**Purse:** $40 million ($10 million winner’s share)

![Image 3: PGA Tour Live on ESPN+ 2025 promotion](https://golf.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/pga-tour-live-2025.jpg)

#### Get ESPN+

With an ESPN+ subscription, you gain access to PGA Tour Live, where you can stream the best PGA Tour events live from wherever you want.

[$11.99/month from ESPN+](https://go.web.plus.espn.com/c/3208296/931309/9070)

### How to watch on TV

NBC and Golf Channel will carry TV coverage of the 2025 Tour Championship this week. Check out the full TV schedule below.

**Thursday, August 21:** 1-6 p.m. ET (Golf Channel)  
**Friday, August 22:** 10 a.m.-3 p.m. ET (Golf Channel)  
**Saturday, August 23:** 1-2:30 p.m. ET (Golf Channel); 2:30-7 p.m. ET (NBC/[Peacock](https://fave.co/45l5EmB))  
**Sunday, August 24:** 12-1:30 p.m. ET (Golf Channel); 1:30-6 p.m. ET (NBC/[Peacock](https://fave.co/45l5EmB))

### How to watch online, streaming

You can watch the 2025 Tour Championship online in multiple ways. [PGA Tour Live on ESPN+](https://go.web.plus.espn.com/c/3208296/931309/9070) will provide exclusive early coverage and featured group coverage all four days of the tournament starting on 11 a.m. ET on Thursday and Sunday, 11:15 a.m. ET on Friday and 12 p.m. ET on Saturday.

[Peacock](https://fave.co/45l5EmB) will provide a live stream of NBC’s Tour Championship coverage, while NBCSports.com and the NBC Sports App will offer live simulcasts of Golf Channel’s telecasts.

Tour Championship 2025: East Lake course guide, start time and how to watch
===========================================================================

Course details for East Lake Golf Club, which hosts the Tour Championship on the PGA Tour. Key stats, weather forecast and more
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 35: Scottie Scheffler with the FedEx Cup trophy at East Lake Golf Club last season](https://www.racingpost.com/_next/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fs3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com%2Fprod-media-racingpost%2Fprod%2Fimages%2F169_1008%2F4365dde38060-gettyimages-2170658393.jpg&w=3840&q=75)

Scottie Scheffler with the FedEx Cup trophy at East Lake Golf Club last season Credit: PGA TOUR

Where is the Tour Championship?
-------------------------------

The BMW Championship will be held at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, Georgia.

When does the Tour Championship start?
--------------------------------------

Georgia is five hours behind the UK and Ireland. The first group is set to tee off at 4.26pm BST on Thursday.

Tour Championship 2025 key details and TV coverage
--------------------------------------------------

The Tour Championship will be shown live on Sky Sports Golf from 6pm on Thursday

East Lake GC course details
---------------------------

### Length

7,440 yards

**Par 70** – Two par-five holes; 12 par-fours; four par-threes

### Course type

Parkland

* * *

### Course records

**72 holes**257 Tiger Woods (2007)**18 holes** 60 Zach Johnson (2007)

### Course winners taking part

Rory McIlroy (three times), Patrick Cantlay, Viktor Hovland, Scottie Scheffler

### Course overview

East Lake is the curtain-closer to the PGA Tour season, with the most successful performers of the year ending their Stateside campaign in the Tour Championship.

East Lake has hosted this event in 1998, 2000, 2002 and from 2004 onwards. The famous course was designed by Tom Bendelow and Donald Ross, but Rees Jones took charge of a redesign in 1994 and at the end of 2007 (he switched all greens from bentgrass to Bermuda), and an even more extensive redesign took place before last year's Tour Championship, with bunkers relocated and reshaped, trees removed, mounds added, and all 18 greens revised, with many much larger and more undulating than before. Andrew Green took charge of that project.

The par changed from 70 to 71 for 2024, with the 14th playing as a par five, but that has been made a par four for this edition, meaning the overall par is back to 70.

A SubAir drainage system means firm, fast greens are almost certain. A handicap system was in place from 2019 through 2024, meaning the FedEx Cup leader started with a two-shot Tour Championship lead, and some players started ten shots behind, but that has been scrapped this year, so everyone starts on the same score

![Image 36: East Lake Golf Club](https://www.racingpost.com/_next/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fs3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com%2Fprod-media-racingpost%2Fprod%2Fimages%2F169_1008%2F36ed4d67cd9a-gettyimages-2170658293.jpg&w=3840&q=75)

East Lake Golf Club Credit: PGA TOUR

What will it take to win the Tour Championship?
-----------------------------------------------

Finding fairways has traditionally been extremely difficult at East Lake. The course was dramatically redesigned prior to last year's event, so previous course form counts for less, but strong ball-striking remains the key to success

### **East Lake Golf Club key attribute**

Accuracy

Tour Championship key stat
--------------------------

The last seven FedEx Cup champions finished eighth or better in one of the preceding playoff events

Tour Championship weather forecast
----------------------------------

Sunny, warm and calm for the most part, but there is a thunderstorm threat on Thursday, Friday and Saturday, so tee-times may be changed to miss them.

What is the prize money for the Tour Championship?
--------------------------------------------------

$40m ($10m to the winner)

Who is in the field for the Tour Championship?
----------------------------------------------

### Field size

The top 30 in the FedEx Cup standings will contest the Tour Championship.

### Highest-ranked players in field (world ranking in brackets)

Scottie Scheffler (1), Rory McIlroy (2), Xander Schauffele (3), Russell Henley (4), Justin Thomas (5)

### The cut

There will be no cut.

Who won the 2024 Tour Championship?
-----------------------------------

Scottie Scheffler built on his handicap start to win the FedEx Cup for the first time. Collin Morikawa carded the lowest 72-hole score, but finished four shots behind Scheffler due to the handicap system.

**BMW Championship** 1 S Scheffler (5-2), 2 R MacIntyre (55-1), 3 M McNealy (50-1), T4 T Fleetwood (20-1), S Burns (35-1), 6 H Hall (55-1).

![](https://wy-static.wenxiaobai.com/10008717094278955026/10008717094278955026.pdf-0-1.png)

**2025 TOUR Championship**
_**(Final event of the FedExCup Playoffs)**_

**Atlanta, Georgia** **August 21-24, 2025** **Purse: $40 million**
**East Lake Golf Club** **Par/Yards: 35-35–70/7,440** **Winner: $10 million**


**Pre-Tournament Information – 2025 TOUR Championship**

**Player Interviews (all times local ET)**
**Tuesday, August 19**
2 p.m. - Tommy Fleetwood
3 p.m. - Justin Thomas

**TBD**

Scottie Scheffler

Rory McIlroy
J.J. Spaun
Harris English

_[*Visit pgatourmedia.com for the latest interview schedule](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/link.mediaoutreach.meltwater.com/ls/click?upn=u001.nowvR4mZSHcec4FW2Kjb8QwlwurJ0qJG8JiW0ejA-2BYHJgw3DgO7Zyx64kGiOwBjcNGwg_Nx8gMnb672aW-2BcXyHMKbOhOJbHvuHLaC6fzqGvP2J4eJUf2x4rxCY4EdkxX3dMqjrq8C8xqTapKd62H1VQU89NMSG7T430eypAWYqfy55IotB-2F-2F0GO84ONwJJYlubiupMFivSbVYqzK8V4jYjFgd7kqiRvlGmqiASuH8pJ3tpDOx15aZyLKQwf9tWZRhNpBmgOQi8yKRH1cQ2FR0R-2BUWkPKmwV3dUu-2FQ2GIoEYHcVKq6m-2FdI6KdkgsO57nbb7RGWmvOEvUEjRTSQv7ABGsdJbNiJT7oJLYEQ-2FKuAIEHjrCnymt2uZrsRVcMfU90T53J-2FsMTblEe098Z1PLvNcAnl-2Bc1-2BTXNxDiCnEFkYKi506Xn1HcEtsWZAqG3XCmPaUTPGAfZlt2jvV82RLqKDDXBgkg-3D-3D__;!!EuSotcx3mN0!N_3MV5ZSs6yQgpnsh6caEAQuM6dITWt7RgkNByDbssjZpbtyWAWVmDXVvgMcGx4TLEeVMB3xPuGdrvW768Sywl4rnc4A$)_

**Scottie Scheffler**


  - World No. 1 and reigning FedExCup Champion seeks to become first back-to-back winner of the FedExCup

  - Enters the TOUR Championship No. 1 in the FedExCup standings for the fourth consecutive year

  - With a win, would join Tiger Woods (2007, 2009) and Rory McIlroy (2016, 2019, 2022) as the only players to win
multiple FedExCup titles

  - Finished inside the top 25 in all 18 starts this season, with a season-high 15 top-10 finishes (including 13 straight
entering the TOUR Championship); last finish outside the top 10 was THE PLAYERS Championship (T20)

  - Leads all players with five wins this season: THE CJ CUP Byron Nelson, PGA Championship, the Memorial
Tournament presented by Workday, The Open Championship, BMW Championship

  - Following his win at last week’s BMW Championship, became the first player since Tiger Woods (2005-07) to
record five or more wins in back-to-back seasons; one of 18 players to win multiple FedExCup Playoffs events
(2024 TOUR Championship, 2025 BMW Championship)

  - Finishes in five prior starts in the TOUR Championship: 2024/Won, 2023/T6, 2022/T2, 2021/T22, 2020/5 [th]

**Rory McIlroy**

  - Only three-time winner of the FedExCup (2016, 2019, 2022) enters the week No. 2 in the FedExCup standings

  - Marks his eighth consecutive season advancing to the TOUR Championship, the longest active streak by any player
(previous: 8/Xander Schauffele, Tony Finau/2017-2024)

  - In 15 starts on TOUR this season, recorded eight top-10 finishes and three wins (AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am, THE
PLAYERS Championship, Masters Tournament)

  - Became the sixth player to complete the Career Grand Slam when he claimed the Masters Tournament this season

  - Eight consecutive seasons with a win is the longest active streak on TOUR

  - Finishes in 11 prior starts in the TOUR Championship: 2024/T9, 2023/4 [th], 2022/Won, 2021/T14, 2020/T8,
2019/Won, 2018/T7, 2016/Won, 2015/T16, 2014/T2, 2012/T10

**J.J. Spaun**

  - Enters the week No. 3 in the FedExCup standings, making his TOUR Championship debut in his ninth season

  - Qualified for the Playoffs for the sixth time in his career (2017, 2018, 2019, 2022, 2023, 2025)

  - Recorded six top-10 finishes in 22 starts this season, highlighted by a win at the U.S. Open, his first win on TOUR
since the 2022 Valero Texas Open


  - Five top-three finishes this season are the second most by any player (Scottie Scheffler/7): T3/Sony Open in
Hawaii, T2/Cognizant Classic in The Palm Beaches, P2/THE PLAYERS Championship, Won/U.S. Open, P2/FedEx St.
Jude Championship

  - Following his runner-up finish at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, became one of three players to secure an
automatic qualification for the U.S. Team in the 2025 Ryder Cup (others: Scottie Scheffler, Xander Schauffele)

  - Prior to this year, best career finish in the FedExCup was 34 [th] (2021-22)

**Justin Thomas**


  - 2017 FedExCup champion making his ninth career appearance in the TOUR Championship

  - Captured his 16 [th] win on TOUR in his 250 [th] career start at the 2025 RBC Heritage

  - In 19 starts this season, recorded seven top-10s, including one win and three runner-up finishes (2 [nd] /The American
Express, 2 [nd] /Valspar Championship, T2/Truist Championship)

  - Four of his seven top-10 finishes this year came in Signature Events: T9/The Genesis Invitational, Won/RBC
Heritage, T2/Truist Championship, T9/Travelers Championship

  - Finishes in eight prior starts in the TOUR Championship: 2024/T14, 2022/T5, 2021/4 [th], 2020/T2, 2019/T3, 2018/T7,
2017/2 [nd], 2016/T6

**Tommy Fleetwood**

  - Enters the week No. 5 in the FedExCup standings, the highest-ranked player in the FedExCup without a win this

season

  - Finished T4 and T3 in the first two Playoffs events, respectively

  - Fifth TOUR Championship appearance and his third consecutive (best finish: T6/2023)

  - Seven top-10s this season are his second-highest total on TOUR since 2017-18 (9/2023)

  - One of two players in the field without a victory on the PGA TOUR (other: Jacob Bridgeman)

**Harris English**


  - Making his fourth career TOUR Championship appearance and first since 2021

  - Four top-10s in 20 starts this season, including his fifth career PGA TOUR title at the Farmers Insurance Open,
runner-up finishes at the PGA Championship and The Open Championship, and a T4 at the Travelers Championship

  - Best career finish in the FedExCup: 12 [th] /2019-20

**TOUR Championship notes:**

  - Beginning this year, Starting Strokes will be eliminated as the TOUR Championship will be played as a 72-hole
stroke-play event, with all players starting the tournament at even par and the winner claiming the FedExCup.

  - The $40 million purse at the TOUR Championship ($10 million to the winner) will count as Official Money for the

first time since 2018

  - Six past FedExCup Champions are in the field: **Scottie Scheffler** (2024), **Viktor Hovland** (2023), **Rory McIlroy** (2016,
2019, 2022), **Patrick Cantlay** (2021), **Justin Rose** (2018), **Justin Thomas** (2017); three former FedExCup Champions
enter the week inside the top five in the FedExCup standings (No. 1/ **Scottie Scheffler**, No. 2/ **Rory McIlroy,** No.
4/ **Justin Rose** )

  - Seven players are making their TOUR Championship debut this week:

`o` **J.J. Spaun** (No. 3), **Ben Griffin** (No. 7), **Maverick McNealy** (No. 10), **Andrew Novak** (No. 15), **Harry Hall**
(No. 26), **Jacob Bridgeman** (No. 27), **Chris Gotterup** (No. 29)

  - 2018 FedExCup Champion **Justin Rose** entered the playoffs ranked 25 [th] in the standings and now sits No. 4
following a win at the FedEx St. Jude Championship and T30 at the BMW Championship

  - **Cameron Young** is making his second TOUR Championship appearance (2022/19 [th] ); claimed his maiden victory on
TOUR at the 2025 Wyndham Championship, becoming the 1,000 [th] unique winner in PGA TOUR history

  - **Hideki Matsuyama** is making his 11 [th] start in the TOUR Championship where he owns a pair of top-five finishes
(2018/T4, 2016/5 [th] )

**FedExCup Playoffs:**

  - Despite not winning an event this season, eight players earned a two-year exemption on TOUR (thru 2027 season)
by advancing to the TOUR Championship: **Tommy Fleetwood** (No. 5), **Maverick McNealy** (No. 10), **Corey Conners**
(No. 19), **Shane Lowry** (No. 24), **Harry Hall** (No. 26), **Jacob Bridgeman** (No. 27), **Sungjae Im** (No. 28), **Akshay Bhatia**
(No. 30)

  - Three players in the field finished inside the top 10 in each of the first two FedExCup Playoffs events: **Scottie**
**Scheffler** (T3-1 [st] ), **Tommy Fleetwood** (T4-T3), **Ludvig Åberg** (T9-T7).


- Of the 12 first-time winners in 2025, 10 qualified for the FedExCup Playoffs, with three advancing to the TOUR
Championship: **Ben Griffin/Andrew Novak** (Zurich Classic of New Orleans), **Cameron Young** (Wyndham
Championship)

- No 2025 rookies qualified for the TOUR Championship this season; of the 35 rookies on TOUR this season, South
Africa’s Aldrich Potgieter was the only one to qualify for the playoffs (No. 52 in the FedExCup standings)

- The FedExCup Bonus Distribution total is $100 million, with the FedExCup Champion earning $10 million

`o` The top 70 players in the FedExCup standings are fully exempt for all Full-Field Events and THE PLAYERS
Championship in 2026
`o` The top 50 players are exempt for all Signature Events in 2026
`o` The top 30 players receive a two-year exemption and invitations to majors that traditionally recognize the
top 30

|---|---|---|---|

PGA Tour eliminates starting-strokes format at Tour Championship
================================================================

*   ![Image 2](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/columnists/full/schlabach_mark.png&h=80&w=80&scale=crop)
    
    Mark SchlabachMay 27, 2025, 07:28 PM ET
    
    [Close](https://www.espn.com/golf/story/_/id/45350150/pga-tour-eliminates-starting-strokes-format-tour-championship#)
    
    *   Senior college football writer
    *   Author of seven books on college football
    *   Graduate of the University of Georgia
    
    [Follow on X](http://twitter.com/intent/user?screen_name=Mark_Schlabach)
    

*   [![Image 3: Copy Link](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/content-reactions/check.png&h=80&w=80)](https://www.espn.com/golf/story/_/id/45350150/pga-tour-eliminates-starting-strokes-format-tour-championship#)
*   [Email](mailto:?subject=PGA%20Tour%20eliminates%20starting%2Dstrokes%20format%20at%20Tour%20Championship&body=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.espn.com%2Fgolf%2Fstory%2F_%2Fid%2F45350150)
*   [Print](https://www.espn.com/espn/print?id=45350150)

Open Extended Reactions

The PGA Tour is eliminating the controversial starting-strokes format from the Tour Championship in its latest attempt to make its season-ending tournament more compelling and climactic for golf fans, the tour announced Tuesday.

Starting with this year's Tour Championship at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta from Aug. 21 to 24, all 30 players in the field will start at even par in a stroke-play tournament.

The winner after 72 holes will capture the FedEx Cup and collect a bonus and five-year PGA Tour exemption.

The PGA Tour's Player Advisory Council (PAC) and policy board approved the changes Tuesday.

"Our Fan Forward Initiative has helped us evaluate each part of the PGA Tour season and today's announcement is an important first step in the evolution of our postseason," PGA Tour commissioner Jay Monahan said in a statement. "The Player Advisory Council led a thorough process to respond to what our fans are asking for: The most competitive golf in the world, played for the highest stakes, in the most straightforward and engaging format."

The PGA Tour considered other ways to play the Tour Championship, including a bracket-style format with head-to-head play. The tour said the PAC would continue to examine the field size and qualification standards for future Tour Championships.

In a news release Tuesday, the tour said golf fans indicated they wanted to see winning scores closer to par at the Tour Championship.

The tour said bonuses for the top 30 golfers in the FedEx Cup standings "will be balanced for 2025 to account for the increased volatility, reward season-long performance and recognize the significance of the FedExCup."

"As the PGA Tour continues to evolve and respond to feedback from fans and players, additional enhancements to the Tour Championship are being evaluated and will be announced in the coming months," the news release said.

The tour is also weighing whether to relocate the Tour Championship to another golf club after the 2027 season, sources told ESPN, although East Lake Golf Club could remain part of a rotation for the event.

Last year, world No. 1 [Scottie Scheffler](http://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/9478/scottie-scheffler) started the tournament at 10 under as the FedEx Cup seasonlong points leader. He was 20 under over 72 holes on his own, and his overall scoring total of 30 under was four strokes better than [Collin Morikawa](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/10592/collin-morikawa), who started at 4 under.

The PGA Tour said its rules committee will "adjust its course setup approach to encourage more risk/reward moments throughout each round, further heightening the drama and competition."

"We want the Tour Championship to be the hardest tournament to qualify for and the FedEx Cup trophy the most difficult to win," Scheffler, a PAC member, said in a statement. "Shifting the Tour Championship to a more straight-up format with a tougher course setup makes it easier for fans to follow and provides a more challenging test for players-which brings out the best competition."

From 2007 to 2018, the PGA Tour crowned two champions at the Tour Championship: the winner of the tournament and the leader in the seasonlong FedEx Cup points race. Starting strokes were introduced in 2019 to protect golfers at the top, while eliminating the confusion of having two champions after the season-ending championship.

The points leader started at 10 under and was at least two strokes ahead of everyone else in the field. The No. 2 player in points started at 8 under, No. 3 at 7 under, No. 4 at 6 under, and so on.

PGA Tour members, including Scheffler, criticized the format as being too gimmicky. Other golfers complained that they didn't have a chance to win the tournament because they were starting so far behind.

"I talked about it the last few years, I think it's silly," Scheffler said during a news conference at the 2024 FedEx St. Jude Championship. "You can't call it a seasonlong race and have it come down to one tournament.

"Hypothetically, we get to East Lake and my neck flares up and it doesn't heal the way it did at the Players. I finish 30th in the FedEx Cup because I had to withdraw from the last tournament? Is that really the seasonlong race? No, it is what it is."

Starting so far in front of the field didn't always guarantee Scheffler a victory. In 2022, he squandered a six-stroke lead by carding a 3-over 73 in the final round and lost to [Rory McIlroy](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/3470/rory-mcilroy) by one. The next year, Scheffler started at 10 under and went just 1 under over 72 holes on his own. He tied for sixth at 11 under, 16 strokes behind winner [Viktor Hovland](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/436487/viktor-hovland).

2025 Tour Championship leaderboard: Russell Henley shoots 61, edges Scottie Scheffler to stand tall in Round 1
==============================================================================================================

Henley shot a flawless 61 to open the Tour Championship two shots up on the No. 1 player in the world.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[![Image 210: Patrick McDonald ](https://sportshub.cbsistatic.com/i/r/2025/11/11/acc97b44-6e88-46ac-838e-a1f4dac5bc8d/thumbnail/80x80/69f6b66523ac2aaff6304e56739f7182/screenshot-2025-11-11-at-11-17-05-am.png)](https://www.cbssports.com/writers/patrick-mcdonald/)

By [Patrick McDonald](https://www.cbssports.com/writers/patrick-mcdonald/)

Aug 21, 2025 at 6:13 pm ET • 1 min read

Join the Conversation

Russell Henley ran wild around East Lake Golf Club in the first round of the 2025 Tour Championship, and in the process, he ran to the top of the leaderboard in the final leg of the FedEx Cup Playoffs. The Georgia native carded seven birdies and an eagle against no dropped shots to piece together a flawless 9-under 61, commanding a two-stroke lead over world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler and a three-stroke lead over Tommy Fleetwood, Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Patrick Cantlay and Robert MacIntyre through the first 18 holes of the season finale.

Henley made 207 feet of putts in his opening refrain, the most of his PGA Tour career and the largest distnce at East Lake since 2004, according to Justin Ray. He knocked in putts from 42 feet, 45 feet and 37 feet -- plus nine other efforts from outside 5 feet -- en route to gaining more than five strokes with the putter and just about six total strokes on the field.

"I just felt like I was at peace if I missed. I felt like I was clear on my reads," Henley said. "Last week, I felt like I played really well and didn't give myself a bunch of looks because I couldn't figure out how far the ball was going and struggled a little bit on the looks of those greens, getting the reads down.

"Just felt a little more clear in my mind on what I thought the ball was going to do and just felt like, yeah, at peace if I missed it. Just kind of free-wheeled it a little bit."

The world No. 4 started his day with four straight pars before he caught fire on the dance floor. Henley put 10 3s on his scorecard over his next 14 holes, including an eagle on the par-5 6th and back-to-back 3s on Nos. 16-17, the latter of which made more than a fair share of players look foolish. One last conversion from inside 12 feet on the last made his personal-best day on the greens official, putting the finishing touches on a career-low round.

Henley's consistency has long made him a worthy FedEx Cup contender, but there is still a long way to go in Atlanta with 54 holes remaining against the tightest, strongest field on the PGA Tour this season. Henley stands in front of a clustered chasing pack filled with major champions and big-time winners, including the man he teamed up with at last year's Presidents Cup (and presumably will at next month's Ryder Cup, too) in Scheffler.

The reigning FedEx Cup champion was up to his usual business Thursday alongside three-time FedEx Cup champion Rory McIlroy. Scheffler started with three birdies in his first six holes before he picked off a couple more as he meandered through his round.

Scheffler was coasting until the end and showed off what separates himself from the rest of the world. Missing his first fairway on No. 16 and settling in hypothetical jail behind a tree, he short sided himself with his second. Taking his medicine and chipping the ball 25 feet beyond the pin, the world No. 1 rolled in his par putt to keep his card clean of any mistakes.

A connection from a similar range came calling on the next hole, but this time for birdie as Scheffler stormed down the hill towards the clubhouse as the skies darkened behind him with potential rains. Taking advantage of the par-5 finisher, the four-time major champion finished with a 63 -- his 18th straight round in the 60s -- just the latest tournament day ending with his name near the top of the leaderboard.

The leader
----------

**1\. Russell Henley (-9):** Henley finished the 2024 Tour Championship with final-round 62 and picked up where he left off Thursday at East Lake. The Arnold Palmer Invitational winner went about his round in a way that is not seen too often on the PGA Tour these days. He ranked last in terms of driving distance but consistently found the short grass and took his chances when he had them. It was a round that perfectly encapsulated who Henley is as a player as he never tried to chew off too much and the birdies kept on flying when he found the stroke with the putter.

"I felt like with it being lift, clean and place and somewhat soft compared to last year when the greens were brand new, it was a little bit softer, so it was just a little bit more gettable," he said.

Contenders
----------

**2\. Scottie Scheffler (-7)  
T3. Collin Morikawa, Patrick Cantlay, Justin Thomas, Robert MacIntyre, Tommy Fleetwood (-6)  
T8. Akshay Bhatia, Ludvig Åberg, Ben Griffin, Rory McIlroy (-4)**

It felt like everyone was making putts in Round 1, but that could not be more true for someone like Morikawa. Experiencing a brutal summer with the putter, the two-time major champion credited some early week work on the greens en route to gaining just about three strokes with the flat stick Thursday. It has positioned the two-time major champion to capture his second top 10 since The Players and perhaps his first win in nearly two years.

"Speed, a lot of speed. It's tough because I look back at the last two weeks and I made nothing," Morikawa said. "But I look at this week and the last two days, I've worked so much on trying to match up my speed to my feel. It's so interesting, when I palm my putter, my speed is impeccable yet I lose a little bit of control. And I'm not going to palm my putter to go and putt out there just because I felt like if I pushed or pulled a putt it would kind of lose that.

"So, it was just how do I match that speed to what I'm seeing. It's just being able to look at the putt in maybe a slightly different view, but grain helps out here a lot for me, which is really nice."

Could a first-timer win the FedEx Cup?
--------------------------------------

Of the 30 players who qualified for the Tour Championship, 12 of them did so without having won a tournament all season. Instead relying on consistency, this crop of competitors has a chance to win just one tournament in 2025 -- the biggest regulation event of the season. Morikawa, Cantlay, MacIntyre and Fleetwood are all on the first page of the leaderboard, but it also other outsiders are similarly playing well through 18 holes. Bubble boy Akshay Bhatia, who got into the Tour Championship thanks to Viktor Hovland making a birdie on the 72nd hole at the BMW Championship, started strong with a 66. Jacob Bridgeman also occupies a place inside the top 10 looking for not only his first win this year but the first of his career.

30.title: Fleetwood and Henley Share Halfway Lead at 2025 TOUR Championship
30.description: ATLANTA, GA – Tommy Fleetwood has surged into a share of the lead at the 2025 TOUR Championship at East Lake Golf Club, posting blistering rounds of 64 and 63 to reach 13-under par at the halfway point. The Englishman was tied with Georgia native Russell Henley, who opened with…

![Image 21: 2025 Tour Championship Tommy Fleetwood](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/PGW-2025-Tour-Championship-Tommy-Fleetwood.jpg)

Tommy Fleetwood of England plays a tee shot on the fourth hole during the second round of TOUR Championship at East Lake Golf Club on August 22, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Ben Jared for PGA TOUR via Getty Images)

ATLANTA, GA – **Tommy Fleetwood** has surged into a share of the lead at the 2025 TOUR Championship at East Lake Golf Club, posting blistering rounds of 64 and 63 to reach 13-under par at the halfway point. The Englishman was tied with Georgia native **Russell Henley**, who opened with a stunning 9-under 61 and chased with a 66, setting the stage for a thrilling weekend in the PGA Tour’s 2025 finale.

Fleetwood, still in search of his maiden PGA Tour victory, showcased his precision and consistency, carding just two bogeys across the first two rounds. His 63 on Friday included a six-pack of birdies on the back nine, capitalizing on the soft conditions at East Lake.

Henley continued his hot putting on Friday, one-putting six of his last seven holes in the opening round and adding five birdies in the second to stay neck-and-neck with Fleetwood.

**Cameron Young** was alone in third after a low-round 62, featuring nine birdies, highlighted by five gains in a six-hole span (Nos. 11-16), to reach 11 under.

One further back was the duo of **Robert MacIntyre** and **Patrick Cantlay**, who posted matching 64s and were deadlocked at 10 under.

[![Image 22: 2025 Tour Championship Scottie Scheffler](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/PGW-2025-Tour-Championship-Scottie-Scheffler.jpg)](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/PGW-2025-Tour-Championship-Scottie-Scheffler.jpg)

Scottie Scheffler and his caddie, Ted Scott, fist bump on the 18th green during the second round of the TOUR Championship 2025 at East Lake Golf Club on August 22, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton via Getty Images)

World No. 1 **Scottie Scheffler** lurks five shots back at 8-under following rounds of 63 and 69, while **Shane Lowry** (63), **Chris Gotterup** (63), **Sam Burns** (66), **Rory McIlroy** (67), **Ben Griffin** (67), **Akshay Bhatia** (67), and **Justin Thomas** (69) were tied at 7 under.

With the FedEx Cup title and a $40 million purse on the line, the leaderboard promises a fierce battle over the final 36 holes.

Cantlay, Fleetwood share lead going into final round of Tour Championship
=========================================================================

Winner of FedEx Cup at East Lake gets $10 million payoff

![Image 2: Patrick Cantlay walks on the 18th green during the third round of the Tour Championship golf tournament, Saturday, Aug. 23, 2025, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)](https://images.ajc.com/resizer/v2/XABRZUPWCJCQPAE2YVO7RWOQV4.jpg?auth=e55fd72ba6e02adba2d5dc6c012a77584d6dfced10e1c55e3ab05090db2b0276&width=3840&height=2160&smart=true)

Patrick Cantlay walks on the 18th green during the third round of the Tour Championship golf tournament, Saturday, Aug. 23, 2025, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)

By Stan Awtrey

Aug 24, 2025

[](https://www.facebook.com/share.php?u=https://www.ajc.com/sports/2025/08/cantlay-fleetwood-share-lead-going-into-final-round-of-tour-championship/)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/2025/08/cantlay-fleetwood-share-lead-going-into-final-round-of-tour-championship/&text=Cantlay%2C%20Fleetwood%20share%20lead%20going%20into%20final%20round%20of%20Tour%20Championship)link copied

Tommy Fleetwood and Patrick Cantlay have a good opportunity to end their winning droughts on Sunday when they take a share of the lead into the final of the Tour Championship.

Fleetwood, who won the DP World Tour’s Dubai Invitational earlier this year, is looking for his first career victory on the PGA Tour. Cantlay, who won the FedEx Cup in 2021, is trying to win for the first time since 2022 and the ninth time in his career.

*   ![Image 1](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/columnists/full/schlabach_mark.png&h=80&w=80&scale=crop)
    
    Mark SchlabachAug 24, 2025, 06:03 PM ET
    
    [Close](https://www.espn.com/golf/story/_/id/46066199/fleetwood-wins-tour-championship-first-pga-tour-title#)
    
    *   Senior college football writer
    *   Author of seven books on college football
    *   Graduate of the University of Georgia
    

ATLANTA -- [Tommy Fleetwood](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/5539/tommy-fleetwood)'s long nightmare is over.

Following so many near misses, the English golfer finally picked up his first PGA Tour victory Sunday after posting a 2-under 68 to finish 18 under in the Tour Championship, three strokes ahead of [Russell Henley](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/5409/russell-henley) and [Patrick Cantlay](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/6007/patrick-cantlay) at East Lake Golf Club.

It was Fleetwood's 164th career start on the PGA Tour, and his long wait, while agonizingly painful and frustrating at times, was well worth it. He collected the FedEx Cup and $10 million for winning.

"It's easy for anybody to say that they are resilient, that they bounce back, that they have fight," Fleetwood said. "It's different when you actually have to prove it."

Though Fleetwood, 34, had won seven times on the DP World Tour and three other times around the world, he had yet to lift a trophy in a PGA Tour event -- until Sunday.

"It shows how great of an attitude he has towards the game, how resilient he is," [Rory McIlroy](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/3470/rory-mcilroy) said after posting an even-par 70 to tie for 23rd at 6 under. "If he gets it done today, that would be amazing. I think we'd all love him to."

It's not that Fleetwood wasn't close previously. His 30 top-five finishes without a victory were the most on the PGA Tour in the past 100 years, according to ESPN Research. His $33.4 million in career earnings were the most for a golfer who hadn't won on tour.

"I never really felt like it wouldn't happen," Fleetwood said. "But there's always doubt there."

Two of Fleetwood's close calls came in the past two months. At the Travelers Championship in Cromwell, Connecticut, on June 22, he led by a shot going into the 72nd hole but three-putted and lost to [Keegan Bradley](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/4513/keegan-bradley) by one.

"I'm upset now," Fleetwood said at the time. "I'm angry. ... It hurts."

At the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis two weeks ago, Fleetwood had a two-shot lead with three holes to play in the first leg of the playoffs. He went 1 over down the stretch. [Justin Rose](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/569/justin-rose) beat [J.J. Spaun](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/10166/jj-spaun) in a playoff, while Fleetwood tied for third.

"Winning on the PGA Tour was a step that I really wanted to take," Fleetwood said. "You don't need anything, but I wanted it. I wanted to do it. It sort of completes the story of the near misses."

It wasn't nearly as dramatic Sunday. After Fleetwood made a bogey on the 10th hole to cut his lead over Cantlay to one stroke, he carded birdies on Nos. 12 and 13 to go back up three. Fleetwood had a three-stroke lead on the 18th hole.

Cantlay's bogey on the par-4 16th all but ended his comeback chances.

Fleetwood became the first golfer to capture his first victory in the Tour Championship at East Lake. [Chad Campbell](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/68/chad-campbell) won the 2003 Tour Championship at Champions Golf Club in Houston.

World No. 1 golfer [Scottie Scheffler](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/9478/scottie-scheffler), who was trying to become the first golfer to win the FedEx Cup in back-to-back seasons, had trouble from the start Sunday.

On the opening hole, Scheffler badly pulled his tee shot down the left side. His ball bounced once and shot under a fence and out of bounds. He made a bogey to fall to 11 under, five shots behind Fleetwood.

After another bogey on the par-4 fifth, Scheffler picked up four birdies to get back into the mix. But then disaster struck when he hit his tee shot into the water on the par-3 15th. A double-bogey 5 knocked him out of the hunt.

Scheffler posted a 2-under 68 and tied for fourth at 14 under, his 14th consecutive top-10 finish, which tied [Jack Nicklaus](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/320/jack-nicklaus) (1977) for the longest streak in the past 50 years.

[Corey Conners](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/9126/corey-conners), who carded an 8-under 62 on Sunday, and [Cameron Young](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/4425906/cameron-young) (66) tied for fourth as well.

"I battled all week to give myself a chance," Scheffler said. "I wasn't as sharp as I would have hoped to have. I had a good first round, but outside of that didn't really play my best the first few days. Still gave myself a shot. Just needed a few better swings."

Bradley, the U.S. Ryder Cup captain, started the final round three strokes behind Fleetwood and Cantlay. But he couldn't get much going, either. Bradley was also a victim of the tricky 15th hole when he pushed his tee shot right into the water, leading to a double-bogey 5.

Bradley will announce his six Ryder Cup captain's picks Wednesday. He called the possibility of choosing himself the "biggest decision of my life."

"No matter what decision that I make here, I could have gone the other way easily, no matter what," Bradley said. "The only thing I care about is on Sunday of the Ryder Cup, that we win the Ryder Cup. Then I'll know I made the right decision.

"Until then, I won't know. It's going to be pretty wild. Whatever decision we make, we're going to have to live with it. I love the guys on our team. They're all playing great. It's just really something else. It's awesome."

There hasn't been a playing captain in the Ryder Cup since [Arnold Palmer](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/334/arnold-palmer) led the Americans to a 23-9 rout at East Lake in 1963. Bradley is ranked No. 13 in the Official World Golf Ranking, and only Scheffler has more victories on tour over the past year.

"Nobody wants to win the Ryder Cup more than Keegan Bradley," said [Maverick McNealy](https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/9530/maverick-mcnealy), who is 10th in points and tied for 23rd at 6 under this week. "I know he's going to make the decision that's best for the team. At the end of the day, it comes down to who plays the best golf."

The 2025 Tour Championship Recap
================================

*   on August 24, 2025

[![Image 2](https://pluggedingolf.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/2025-Tour-Championship.png?resize=630%2C420)](https://pluggedingolf.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/2025-Tour-Championship.png)

Atlanta, GA – Tommy Fleetwood has won the 2025 Tour Championship and the FedEx Cup.  This marks his first PGA Tour win.  As one of the most important events of the year, it also comes with the largest prize money, a cool $10 million.

For years, Fleetwood has been one of the most talented professional golfers who has yet to win a PGA Tour event.  As a matter of fact, in his 164 starts, he had secured 29 top-five finishes, which included six second-place finishes, two second-place finishes in major events, and even a silver medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

Today, he was able to push aside the memories of the close calls and was able to close out the tournament with a score of 18-under par, winning by three shots over Patrick Cantlay and Russel Henley, who both finished in a tie for second place with scores of 15-under par.  This makes Fleetwood the first player since Chad Campbell, all the way back in 2003, to earn his first PGA Tour win at the Tour Championship.

World number one Scottie Scheffler had what, for him, was a disappointing week.  His putter wasn’t working to his exacting standards, and yet he would finish in a three-way tie for fourth place at 14-under par with the likes of Cameron Young and Corey Conners.  While all those players would have loved to have won, they will still be walking away with millions of dollars in prize money.

The PGA Tour now takes a bit of a hiatus, where many of the world’s best players will be enjoying a well-deserved break.  The next event on the docket is the Procore Championship in Napa, California, which begins on September 11th.  Patton Kizzire will attempt to defend the title that he won there last year, but will be facing a challenging field.  There, several Ryder Cup team members will be playing to stay fresh for the iconic event, including world number one Scottie Scheffler, Xander Schauffele, and others.

**Tommy Fleetwood’s What’s In The Bag:**
----------------------------------------

**Driver:** [**TaylorMade Qi35**](https://pluggedingolf.com/taylormade-qi35-driver-review/) (10.5°) / [**Fujikura Ventus TR Blue**](https://pluggedingolf.com/fujikura-ventus-tr-shaft-review/) 6 X

**Mini Driver:** [**TaylorMade R7 Quad**](https://pluggedingolf.com/taylormade-r7-quad-mini-driver-review/) (13.5°) / Fujikura Ventus TR Blue 6 X

**5 Wood:** [**TaylorMade Qi35**](https://pluggedingolf.com/taylormade-qi35-fairway-wood-review/) (18°) / Mitsubishi Kuro Kage 80 TX

**9 Wood:** [**TaylorMade Qi10**](https://pluggedingolf.com/taylormade-qi10-fairway-wood-review/) (24°) / Mitsubishi Kuro Kage 80 TX

**Irons:** [**TaylorMade P7TW**](https://pluggedingolf.com/taylormade-p7tw-tiger-woods-irons-review/) (5-PW) / Project X 6.5
